subject: Symphony pilot — cost breakdown & action items
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@symphonylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Symphony pilot — cost breakdown & action items

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a first-pass invoice snapshot attached. Please see the attached Symphony_pilot_costs_v1.xlsx (tabbed: assumptions, hourly/throughput, invoice-snapshots) and a lightweight CSV with scenario runs.

Call highlights / assumptions I used in the model
- Expected traffic for pilot: 1.0M prompt tokens / day (~30M tokens/month) across dev+canary+prod demo traffic.
- Quality target: mid-tier (quantized 8-bit variant); preference for latency < 250ms p50.
- KV cache hit assumed 15% for prefix-heavy flows.

High level cost snapshot (rough)
- Estimated Redwood cost: ~$1,100 per 1M tokens (includes model runtime, infra amortized) at the mid-tier profile.
- Symphony budget range mentioned on call: $25k–$50k/month. With 30M tokens/month that maps to ~$900–$1,700 / 1M tokens depending on batching and cache.

Open questions for you (so we can finalize an invoice sample):
1) Is 1.0M tokens/day a reasonable baseline for the pilot or should I model 0.5M and 2.0M variants?
2) Who should be on the procurement thread for contract/pricing? (I included procure@symphonylabs in case).
3) Any hard requirements on retention / regional isolation (for pricing/kms)?

Next steps I propose
- You confirm traffic baseline + procurement contact.
- We iterate the attached sheet and I’ll produce a two-page invoice snapshot and AMP (mutual-action-plan) PDF for signature.
- If procurement wants, we can run a 2-week canary with 24/7 monitoring; I included a canary column in the sheet.

Attachments: Symphony_pilot_costs_v1.xlsx, redwood-pricing-scenarios.csv

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0149

---
(Attachment stub: Symphony_pilot_costs_v1.xlsx — 120KB spreadsheet; redwood-pricing-scenarios.csv — scenario outputs)

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@symphonylabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@symphonylabs.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Symphony pilot — cost breakdown & action items

Mina — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. The assumptions line up with what we discussed. Additional context:
- The pilot objective is to validate 3 core flows (search assist, summarization, and form autofill). We expect peak days to hit ~1.5–2x baseline but average should be ~1M/day.
- Our procurement lead is Claire Tang (claire.tang@symphonylabs.com) — I copied her on this reply. Claire will need an invoice snapshot + standard SOW language.
- Budget: we have an internal target of $40k/month for the pilot (flexible if the performance delta justifies it).

Can you produce two invoice snapshots:
A) Conservative: 0.8M tokens/day, limited KV cache (5%), single region (us-west)
B) Stretch: 1.2M tokens/day, 20% KV cache, burst capacity for 12h/day (multi-zone)

Also attaching a brief requirements doc — Symphony_requirements.pdf — that lists required retention and PII handling (we can redline if needed).

Happy to jump on another 30-min call next week if that helps.

—Jordan
Jordan Park
Product Lead, Integrations | Symphony Labs
jordan.park@symphonylabs.com

(Attachment stub: Symphony_requirements.pdf — 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Symphony pilot — pricing scenarios and quick ops notes

Mina / Ben — quick notes after scanning the sheet Jordan sent back. I ran the pricing scenarios in redwood-pricing-scenarios.csv (attached) and flagged the most likely invoice bands. Key recommendations: 
- Use the Conservative/Stretch approach Jordan requested. For the conservative case we can target ~$1,000 / 1M tokens after plugging in batching optimizations (we’re assuming 12-token average reply length for the flows).
- For the stretch case with burst capacity, list a separate burst line-item in the invoice (per-hour GPU surcharge) to keep the committed baseline lower but allow headroom.
- Suggest we model an optional 3-month volume discount tier (5% at 500k+/day) — helps close if budget flexibility is tight.

Action items for Mina:
- Add the two scenarios Jordan requested into tab 'invoice-variants' and include a 'canary' run at 50% traffic for 14 days.
- I'll prepare the AMP PDF (pilot_mutual-action-plan.pdf) with milestone dates and success criteria.

Ben — can you confirm the typical SLA language we should include for a pilot (uptime target + p50/p95 latency targets) so I can drop it into the AMP?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

(Attachment stub: redwood-pricing-scenarios.csv — scenario outputs)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@symphonylabs.com>, Claire Tang <claire.tang@symphonylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Symphony pilot — cost breakdown & action items

Thanks Jordan / Claire — copied Marissa and Ben who will own the AMP and SLA pieces. I updated the workbook with the two requested invoice snapshots and added a 14-day canary column. Highlights from the updated sheet:
- Conservative (0.8M/day): estimated invoice = $28,800/month (~$1,200 / 1M tokens); includes single-region, limited KV, no burst.
- Stretch (1.2M/day + burst): estimated invoice = $58,400/month (breaks down to ~$970 / 1M tokens when amortized across baseline + burst hours). Burst is listed as a separate line: $/GPU-hour.

Attachments I’ve generated for your review: pilot_mutual-action-plan.pdf (milestones + signoff), Symphony_pilot_costs_v1.xlsx (tab updated), redwood-pricing-scenarios.csv (scenario outputs). I also exported a two-page invoice snapshot you can pass to procurement (link above).

Proposed next steps
1) Claire — confirm procurement contact details and any PO requirements / legal redlines.
2) Jordan — confirm which scenario you prefer for an initial 30-day pilot. If you pick conservative we can still enable burst with a PO for the first 2 weeks.
3) If yes, we’ll issue an official pilot quote and send the AMP for signature (DocuSign link included in related links).

Would you be available Tuesday 9/21 for a 30-min sync? I can share the invoice snapshot and walk the team through the cost drivers live.

Best —
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
